verdicts.trueWording: I'm smelling what the characters are smelling
verdicts.note: Kobold Press page (Jeremy L.C. Jones, May 26, 2009) fetched raw, HTTP 200. Full passage: "I plunge into the story and imagine that I'm there. I'm smelling what the characters are smelling, tasting what they're—well, you know the rest. What I then have to do is write down enough of what I can see, in my mind's eye, so that any reader will feel they too can see the moldering crypt ... or the glittering court of Zayang the Unimpeachable." Every limb — imagining presence, smelling, tasting, writing enough for the reader to see crypt and court — is on the page. Quote matches word for word (page uses a curly apostrophe).

verdicts.trueWording: I write about what publishers ask me to
verdicts.note: Same Kobold Press page. "I get the chance to get published because I write about what publishers ask me to ... I write about what those who set the assignment want me to. And do so in a way that is entertaining and leaving the reader wanting more." The 'in the way they want it' limb rests on the exam analogy plus the same page's 'constrained by editors, publisher word counts and formats' and 'fitting in (perhaps even to a particular prose style)'; 'entertainingly' is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: never think your words are perfect
verdicts.note: Paizo blog, James L. Sutter, Jun 20, 2013, fetched raw, HTTP 200. Advice-for-writers answer: "rewrite anything that seems weak and awkward ... always work on clearly dated copies, but never think your words are perfect. Don't be afraid to rewrite." Quote is word for word; the page has lowercase 'never' mid-sentence where the claim capitalizes it. Both limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: The text is forced to stand on its own.
verdicts.note: SA-Compendium.pdf fetched (23pp, 'Version 2.7 ©2021 Wizards of the Coast'), text extracted with pypdf. Page 1-2, RAW section: "When I dwell on the RAW interpretation of a rule, I'm studying what the text says in context, without regard to the designers' intent. The text is forced to stand on its own. Whenever I consider a rule, I start with this perspective." Reads-first, in-context, intent-disregarded and stands-on-its-own limbs all present.

verdicts.trueWording: lay a foundation of rules that a DM could build on
verdicts.note: Same PDF, 'The Role of Rules': "no set of rules could reasonably account for every contingency. If the rules tried to do so, the game would become unplayable ... The direction we chose for the current edition was to lay a foundation of rules that a DM could build on, and we embraced the DM's role as the bridge between the things the rules address and the things they don't." Deliberateness ('the direction we chose') is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: are not official rulings; they are advice
verdicts.note: Same PDF, 'Official Rulings': "Official rulings on how to interpret rules are made here in the Sage Advice Compendium ... The public statements of the D&D team, or anyone else at Wizards of the Coast, are not official rulings; they are advice. The tweets of Jeremy Crawford ... are sometimes a preview of rulings that appear here." Both limbs (compendium-only official; tweets/public statements are advice) present verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: appendices summarizes all of the main rules terminology
verdicts.note: D&D Beyond post 1745 fetched raw, HTTP 200; byline 'by Michael Galvis / Sep 17, 2024' matches. "The 2024 Player's Handbook lowers the barrier to entry ... with an expansive play guide. In its early chapters, you'll learn key terms of the game, like what a D20 Test and Magic action are, and find examples of play, such as in combat, with sidebars that break down the game mechanics." The appendix limb is supported by "One of the included appendices summarizes all of the main rules terminology" — substance matches, though the article body never uses the word 'glossary' (that word appears only in site navigation).

verdicts.trueWording: uses some new terms, as shown in the Updated Terminology Table
verdicts.note: D&D Beyond post 1810 fetched raw, HTTP 200; byline 'by DND Staff / Sep 3, 2024' matches. Under 'New Terminology' the Updated Terminology table lists all three named pairs: Race > Species, Cast a Spell action > Magic action, Ki > Monk's Focus (also Ki Points > Focus Points).

verdicts.trueWording: Use bullet points and formatting to draw the DM's eye
verdicts.note: D&D Beyond post 753 fetched raw, HTTP 200; byline 'by Shawn Merwin / Mar 25, 2020' matches. "Use headers and subheaders to call out breaks in information. Use bullet points and formatting to draw the DM's eye to the right information at the right time." All three devices and the DM's-eye purpose are on the page; the page splits the purposes across two sentences (headers/subheaders 'call out breaks in information'; bullets and formatting 'draw the DM's eye'), which the claim merges into one.

verdicts.trueWording: short, evocative, and helpful to the DM and players
verdicts.note: EN World thread page 10 fetched raw, HTTP 200. Post #96 by 'Burnside', Apr 8, 2025: "Boxed text needs to be short, evocative, and helpful to the DM and players." Same post quotes his own 'first published adventure (2018)' boxed text and judges it "filled with excessive detail, irrelevancies, and the area in general has too many distractions/too many little things going on." The 'Goodman Games designer' label rests on the same post's "Area description for something I wrote this year for Goodman Games" plus "something I had to learn as a designer" — no formal title is stated.

verdicts.trueWording: don't want to assume that people have access to the old books
verdicts.note: CBR interview fetched raw, HTTP 200; 'Published Feb 5, 2025'. Crawford: "In all of the books we have coming up, including the Monster Manual, we've made sure to fill them with lore nuggets. Because ... this game's been around for half-a-century, and we love it, but we don't want to assume that people have access to the old books." The page says 'have access to' rather than 'own', and says 'all of the books we have coming up' — broader than, and inclusive of, the 2025 core books (the adjacent paragraph does discuss 'the new Core books').

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that no D&D house style guide is published — the page says nothing about whether the style is published or unpublished
verdicts.trueWording: making sure that everything matched the D&D house style
verdicts.note: Grognardia fetched raw, HTTP 200; 'Wednesday, August 27, 2025', 'Interview: Mike Mearls'. Answer 8: "Ian Pace developed the rules and nailed down the technical end of the manuscript, making sure that everything matched the D&D house style and that our rules synched with the D&D rulebooks." Quote verbatim; the collaborator, the manuscript (Cthulhu by Torchlight, a Chaosium/non-WotC 5e product per the introduction) and the existence of a D&D house style are all supported. The trailing inference 'even where none is published' is the researcher's gloss — the page makes no statement about publication of the style, and items 241-243 of this same chunk cite a circulating WotC style guide.

verdicts.trueWording: takes both of those works as its foundation
verdicts.note: Style guide PDF fetched (11pp) and extracted with pypdf. p.1: "We have two primary resources for the house style of DUNGEONS & DRAGONS products: The Chicago Manual of Style, 17th edition / Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 11th edition. This guide takes both of those works as its foundation, so it focuses on matters of style and spelling that are particular to D&D products, where we depart from or expand on the recommendations of those works." Note on dating: the running header reads 'Version 1.08a ©2018 Wizards of the Coast' and the document text contains no 2019 or January date — the 'updated January 2019' label comes only from the filename, as the source line itself flags. Version number and both style foundations verified.

verdicts.trueWording: apply to all D&D products, whether RPG books, board games, novels
verdicts.note: Same PDF, p.1, section heading 'General Rules': "The rules in this section apply to all D&D products, whether RPG books, board games, novels, or something else." Quote verbatim; the 'not just rulebooks' limb is exactly the page's enumeration.

verdicts.trueWording: we spell out and lowercase references to editions
verdicts.note: Same PDF, rule spans p.1-p.2: "Editions of the RPG. In a departure from previous usage, we spell out and lowercase references to editions of the roleplaying game. We write “fifth edition,” for instance, not “5th Edition.” ... Our internal documentation occasionally uses edition abbreviations like 4E and 5E. In other contexts, such abbreviations should appear only in a table, a conversion document, or in an informal text." Quote verbatim on p.2 as cited; both limbs supported. The page adds one carve-out the claim omits: internal documentation itself does use 4E/5E.
